page: Vultr vcg-a16-12c-128g-32vram is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance configured with 12 shared Intel vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture. The underlying processor configuration consists of 6 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz with hyper-threading enabled, supported by a 16 MB L3 cache. System memory totals 128.0 GB, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 10.67 GB per vCPU. Acceleration is provided by two NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs, delivering a combined 32 GB of VRAM. Local storage is comprised of a 700 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong capabilities in machine learning workloads. For large language model inference using a small 135M model, prompt processing reaches a top-tier rate of 8,665.1 tokens per second, while text generation registers at 260.3 tokens per second. With a medium 7B model, prompt processing achieves 613.27 tokens per second, and text generation operates at 32.35 tokens per second. General compute benchmarks place the instance in the average tier, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 21,080.54 and a PassMark CPU score of 20,085.48. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 1,191.06 GB/sec, which drops to 102.38 GB/sec for large uncached blocks.

The instance offers a specialized hardware profile that balances dual-GPU acceleration with a substantial memory footprint, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring parallel graphics processing and large datasets without the expense of dedicated bare-metal GPU hosts. However, the shared CPU allocation model represents a potential performance tradeoff for sustained, CPU-bound execution. Given these characteristics, the server is suited for small-to-medium large language model inference, graphics rendering, video transcoding, and database operations that benefit from GPU acceleration and NVMe storage.
